data.title: Bank of America Stock (BAC) Drops on Weak Q3 Outlook — Is a Broader Slowdown Coming?
data.description:
Bank of America (BAC) shares fell 5% on Monday after CEO Brian Moynihan warned that its Wall Street businesses could see a weaker third quarter. Speaking at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference, Moynihan said investment banking fees could fall more than 10% year-over-year in Q3 to $1.6 billion-$1.8 billion, while trading revenue is expected to be roughly flat. The outlook is a sharp change from Q2, when Bank of America reported a 50% jump in investment banking fees and a 33% increase in trading revenue.

BAC was the weakest-performing stock in the KBW Bank Index on Monday. Other major bank stocks also fell, with Goldman Sachs (GS) down about 4.1% and Morgan Stanley (MS) down 3.6%, while Citigroup (C) fell 2%.

Is a Broader Wall Street Slowdown Coming?

BofA's weaker outlook may be more than a company-specific issue. Data from Jefferies (JEF) suggests that investment banking activity was already slowing across major banks before BofA issued its warning. As of Sept. 3, investment banking revenue at eight major global banks was down 15% from a year earlier and 27% from Q2, according to Jefferies data.

Meanwhile, Citigroup CFO Gonzalo Luchetti told analysts that investment banking revenue was on track to grow at a "low-single-digit" rate in Q3. Trading revenue was expected to rise at a "mid-single-digit" rate. He said, "September is a key month."

Still, not all banks may feel the impact equally. Goldman Sachs (GS) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) could be better positioned because of their broader investment banking businesses and strong positions in M&A and equity capital markets. This gives them more ways to offset weakness in any one area.

On a positive note, Moynihan pointed to a strong deal pipeline, especially in middle-market investment banking, offering some optimism for future activity.

Is BAC Stock a Buy?

According to the Street's analysts, BAC stock has a Strong Buy rating based on 14 Buys and two Holds assigned in the last three months. Bank of America's stock has an average price target of $68.86, implying 15.7% upside from the current price.

data.title: Stock Futures Fall as Fed Rate-Hike Bets Rise, Oil Prices Climb
data.description:
U.S. stock futures traded lower ahead of Tuesday's session as investors awaited the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday. Markets are pricing in a 92% chance of a 0.25 percentage-point rate hike, which would raise the Fed's target range to 3.75%-4.00%. Meanwhile, the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.02%, while oil prices continued climbing amid rising tensions in the Middle East.

Futures on the Nasdaq 100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were down 0.35%, 0.32%, and 0.40%, respectively, as of 1:46 a.m. EDT on September 15.

Oil prices extended gains on Tuesday as fresh attacks in the Gulf raised concerns about supply disruptions. Saudi Arabia also shut its key East-West oil pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, after drone attacks damaged it, further tightening supply. At the time of writing, Brent crude (CM:BZ) traded near $108.21 a barrel, while WTI crude (CM:CL) was near $103.43 a barrel.

data.title: Broadcom Stock (AVGO) Gained in After-Hours Trading as CEO Dismisses AI Slowdown Fears
data.description:
Broadcom (AVGO) stock edged higher in after-hours trading Monday after CEO Hock Tan dismissed concerns about a slowdown in AI development. The shares closed at $344.72, down 4.77%, but rose about 0.4% after the market closed. Tan's comments came after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower pace of development for advanced AI models.

The comments appear to be giving investors some relief after Monday's sharp sell-off in AI stocks. Tan said the debate over slowing AI development has not changed Broadcom's long-term outlook.

Broadcom CEO Rejects AI Slowdown Concerns

Tan said he has not changed his expectations for Broadcom's AI semiconductor business. When asked whether recent concerns had made him reconsider the company's fiscal 2027 and 2028 forecasts, he gave a direct answer. "No, not in the least," Tan said.

data.title: Waymo Targets 2027 Tokyo Launch in Major Robotaxi Expansion
data.description:
Alphabet's (GOOGL) autonomous-driving unit Waymo is taking its robotaxi ambitions overseas, targeting a commercial launch of fully driverless taxis in Tokyo in 2027. Waymo has partnered with Japanese taxi-app operator GO ($JP:581a) and taxi company Nihon Kotsu to develop Japan's first commercial autonomous taxi service.

The companies plan to initially deploy a small fleet and gradually scale the service to about 100 vehicles, subject to regulatory approvals and safety requirements. Japan's current rules require a human to sit in the driver's seat, even in fully autonomous vehicles.

Waymo Is Going Global

Waymo and its Japanese partners have been testing autonomous vehicles (AVs) on Tokyo's public roads since 2025. The testing has focused on adapting Waymo's self-driving technology to Tokyo's narrow streets and heavy traffic.

Promotion

200% short exposure to AMZN with AMZO

Under the planned commercial service, customers will be able to hail Waymo vehicles through both the GO and Waymo apps. Nihon Kotsu will handle local transportation operations, while GO will help integrate the technology into Japan's existing taxi ecosystem. Waymo will provide its autonomous-driving technology and operational systems.

The Tokyo expansion comes as Waymo accelerates its global robotaxi rollout. The company currently provides more than 500,000 autonomous trips per week across major U.S. markets, according to its website.

Why It Matters for Waymo

Japan could represent an important growth market for Waymo as the country faces a shrinking workforce and persistent shortages of taxi drivers. A successful Tokyo launch could also provide Waymo with a foothold for broader expansion in Japan.

However, the 2027 target remains subject to regulatory and safety approvals. The companies said the commercial launch date will be determined after the necessary permits are secured.

Waymo's Tokyo rollout could mark another important step in expanding the company from a U.S.-focused autonomous-driving business into a global robotaxi platform.

Earlier this year, U.S.-based autonomous-driving startup Nuro began testing its vehicles in Tokyo, marking its first expansion outside the U.S. through partnerships with Uber (UBER) and Lucid Group (LCID). Backed by investors including Nvidia (NVDA) and Toyota (TM), Nuro could emerge as a competitor to Waymo and Amazon's (AMZN) Zoox as competition in the global robotaxi market intensifies.

On TipRanks, GOOGL has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 24 Buys and four Hold ratings. The average Alphabet price target of $425.88 implies 21.9% upside potential from current levels. Year-to-date, GOOGL shares have gained 11.8%.

data.title: President Trump Calls Nvidia's Huang Onstage, Dismisses AI Regulation Concerns
data.description:
President Donald Trump called Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang live on speakerphone at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles on Monday to dismiss growing concerns about AI regulation proposals. The call happened while Huang was speaking at the summit, and he held his phone to the microphone so the crowd could hear the full exchange.

During the five-minute call, Trump dismissed fears of an existential AI takeover as a "hoax." and said robots are not going to take over the world. He argued that slowing U.S. tech development or adding heavy rules on data centers would only help foreign rivals like China.

While Trump noted the U.S. must proceed "prudently," he emphasized that "that doesn't mean we're going to stop an industry." Huang agreed with the president, saying the U.S. can lead in AI while staying safe.

Widening Split Emerging in Tech Sector

The phone call points to a widening split in the tech world. Some leaders, including President Trump, Nvidia's Huang, and Meta's (META) Mark Zuckerberg, say that AI safety fears are overblown and that heavy rules would slow U.S. innovation while giving China an edge.

Others, like Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman, warn that fast‑moving AI systems could pose real cyber and biosecurity risks unless the industry agrees on guardrails and a slower path.

After the event, Trump repeated his stance on social media, calling himself the AI "Hoax Buster" and framing safety warnings as political fear‑driven messaging.

Mizuho Sees the Selloff as a Buying Opportunity

Mizuho said the sharp drop in AI‑linked semis is a buying chance, noting that names like Micron (MU), Lumentum (LITE), Credo (CRDO), SanDisk (SNDK), Broadcom (AVGO), Dell (DELL), and Lam Research (LRCX) still look well-placed.

The firm said calls from Anthropic and OpenAI to slow frontier‑model work have stirred safety worries, but they do not see a real shift in AI data center spend.

Mizuho also argued that guardrail pushes and RSI limits will not work without global alignment and could even hand an advantage to faster Chinese rivals. With the PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) down about 6%, the firm sees the pullback as overdone and expects AI adoption to stay positive for core semi players.

Which AI Stock Is a Better Buy?

According to TipRanks' Stock Comparison Tool, AI stocks such as Micron, Nvidia, Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), Meta, and Microsoft (MSFT) have Strong Buy consensus ratings. Among these stocks, analysts see the most upside in Micron at 69.25%, followed by NVDA at 53.72% and Amazon at 31.84%. GOOGL stock offers 21.89% upside.

data.title: Corning Stock (GLW) Plunged Over 13% on Monday – Here's What Spooked Investors
data.description:
Corning (GLW) shares dropped 13.6% on Monday after the company said it will sell up to $2 billion in new stock through an at‑the‑market program with Goldman Sachs (GS). The slide comes due to a mix of dilution worries and rising fear about AI spending. Following the deal, Mizuho Securities analyst John Roberts, CFA, maintained a Buy rating on GLW stock and cut the price target to $180 from $210.

GLW stock has climbed over 65% so far this year, aided by AI fiber deals and strong demand for optical parts. Thus, the surprise capital raise gave traders a reason to lock in gains.

Corning is a manufacturer of specialty glass, ceramics, and advanced optical products.

Promotion

Two ETFs for long or short leverage on COHR

Details About the Deal

Goldman Sachs is the sole sales agent on the deal. Corning said the net proceeds will go toward general corporate needs, using a shelf registration filed earlier this year. This setup has no set price and no set share count, giving Corning full control over when and how much stock it sells.

This setup is driving the sharp reaction as holders have no clear way to know when new supply might hit the market after a big run‑up in the stock this year.

Capex Gaps and Capital‑Heavy Optical Builds Raise Questions

Roberts noted Corning's long-term Springboard plan calls for strong free cash flow growth, but some parts of the optical business, like glass fiber furnaces, are capital heavy. The equity program looks like a simple backstop to make sure Corning can finish major projects even if customer capex or market conditions shift.

He also said Corning has not shared clear base case capex needs for its 2030 targets, including a 50% boost in glass fiber output. Capital intensity varies across solar wafers, downstream solar, optical cores, and cables, with cables and connectors being the least costly.

AI Spending Jitters Add Sector-Wide Pressure

The optical hardware sector depends on Big Tech's large AI data center budgets. Over the weekend, leaders from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Elon Musk publicly urged slowing frontier AI development.

Even though the leaders did not ask to cut capex, the comments sparked worries that cloud giants may cool hardware spending. That pressure is dragging down other optical names like Coherent (COHR), Fabrinet (FN), and Lumentum (LITE).

Is GLW a Good Stock to Buy Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on GLW stock based on seven Buys and three Holds assigned in the past three months. Further, the average Corning price target of $188.75 per share implies 31.44% upside potential.
